_readme: Add a species by copying one entry. 'vision' links to a mode in script.js (dog, bee, eagle, fly, snake) or leave it as null. IMPORTANT: the 'range' shapes below are rough hand-drawn placeholders. Replace them with real range polygons (IUCN Red List, simplified in mapshaper.org). GeoJSON uses [longitude, latitude] order. Verify every fact and cite it on the sources section before submitting.

species.name: Gray wolf
species.visionNote: Dogs descend from wolf-like ancestors and share the same two-cone colour vision, so the dog view is a good stand-in.
facts: A pack is usually a family: a breeding pair and their offspring.
Dogs are descended from an ancient population of wolves.
Wolves can cover very long distances in a day while hunting or dispersing.

species.name: Western honey bee
species.visionNote: Bees see ultraviolet, blue and green, but not red.
facts: Foragers do a 'waggle dance' that tells nestmates the direction and distance of food.
Many flowers have ultraviolet patterns that guide bees to the nectar.
A summer colony can hold tens of thousands of workers.
species.rangeNote: Native to Europe, Africa and western Asia. The shape shows the native range only. People have introduced it almost everywhere.

species.name: Bald eagle
species.visionNote: Eagles have far sharper eyesight than humans, so the effect is shown as extra sharpness.
facts: Its numbers crashed in the mid-1900s, partly due to the pesticide DDT, then recovered after it was banned.
Raptor eyes have a very dense layer of light sensors and can resolve fine detail from far away.
Pairs build some of the largest nests of any North American bird.

species.name: Housefly
species.visionNote: A compound eye is made of thousands of tiny lenses. Flies also process motion much faster than we do.
facts: Each compound eye is built from thousands of tiny units called ommatidia.
Flies can perceive flicker and fast motion at rates well beyond human limits, which is why they dodge swatters.
They live alongside humans on nearly every continent.
species.rangeNote: Found almost worldwide with people. The shapes are very rough continents.

species.name: Western diamondback rattlesnake
species.visionNote: Pit vipers sense heat through pit organs between the eye and nostril and combine it with normal vision.
facts: Pit organs detect infrared heat, so the snake can sense warm prey in the dark.
The rattle is made of keratin, the same material as your fingernails.
It lives in deserts, scrub and rocky areas of the southwestern US and northern Mexico.
